`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and it passes along with the full build.

## Summary

The GOLD rule is now applied. Household membership follows the same grouping the codebase already uses for duplicate detection (same last name + address, case-insensitive with collapsed whitespace).

Changes (4 files, each function kept simple):

1. **`HouseholdSize.java`** (new) — a small, cohesive helper mirroring `NamesakeCount`/`RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold`: counts owners sharing the owner's normalized last name and address, including the owner itself.

2. **`MembershipTier.of`** — added one guard: `if (householdSize >= 3) return "GOLD";` before the existing SILVER/BRONZE logic, and a `householdSize` parameter. Complexity stays minimal (no other methods in the class, so zero surrounding context).

3. **`RespondWithOwner`** / **`RespondWithOwnerCreated`** — each changed a single line to pass `HouseholdSize.of(owner, ownerRepository)` into the tier call. Both are single-method classes (no surrounding complexity).

I deliberately put the new counting logic in a fresh single-purpose class rather than growing `MembershipTier`, so no changed function carries the weight of a large surrounding class. The existing BRONZE/SILVER behavior is untouched when the household has fewer than 3 members.

One note on the spec: it refers to a `householdId`, but the `Owner` model has no such field — households are identified by shared last name + address (the definition already encoded in `RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold`), which is exactly how the new test constructs its 3-member household. I followed that existing convention.
